AGENDA
PLANNING COMMISSION
MEETING
Upon request, the agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability in compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act. Please contact the City Clerk at (310) 378-0383, at least 48 hours prior to the meeting to request a disability-related modification or accommodation.
Any person who has made campaign contributions to any of the members of the Planning Commission within twelve months before this meeting, should examine the provisions of Government Code Section 84308 which is posted on the bulletin board outside the Council Chamber.
We are advised by the members of the Commission that none of them have received campaign contributions within the last twelve months.
The applicant or any property owner entitled to notice of the hearing may, within fifteen days after the date of the Planning Commission decision, appeal the Planning Commission decision to the City Council (Ord. No. 091-529). A fee is required for filing an appeal with the City Clerkâ€™s office (R05-14).
The Council may, within fifteen days after the date of the decision or on or before the first date following the first Council meeting after the date of the Planning Commission decision, whichever occurs last: 1) Confirm the action of the Planning Commission and grant or deny the application; 2) Set the matter for public hearing and dispose of it in the same manner as on an appeal; or 3) Amend, modify, delete or add any condition of approval which the Council finds is not substantial under the circumstances relative to or affecting the property subject to the application for a development entitlement. Any determination of the Council pursuant to this paragraph shall be conclusive and final.
The Planning Commission reserves the right to modify the order of items shown on the agenda and advises all interested parties to arrive promptly at the commencement of the meeting.

ACTION MINUTES
  PLANNING COMMISSION
  MAY 15, 2018

Council Chambers  Tuesday
City Hall  May 15, 2018
340 Palos Verdes Drive West  6:30 p.m.
Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

CALL TO ORDER

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

ROLL CALL

COMMUNICATIONS FROM PUBLIC - None

CONSENT CALENDAR

Staff proposes the following items for Consent:

1.  NC-1629-18; Consideration of a Neighborhood Compatibility Application for a new single
  family residence located at 720 Paseo Del Mar. Lot 4, Block 1429, Tract 8523. This
  project is exempt from CEQA pursuant to California Administrative Code Title 14, Chapter
  3, Section 15303.

  Applicant/Owner:  Lu Ana & Nelson Bercier

  Action: Commissioner Chang moved and Commissioner Criley seconded to approve the
  application (5-0 in favor) with standard conditions and the following additional condition:
  1) Per LID guidelines, the following measures must be implemented for the design and
  construction of the project:

  a. Divert roof runoff and surface flow to vegetated areas before discharge unless the
  diversion would result in slope instability; and
  b. Direct surface flow to vegetated areas before discharge.

Planning Commission  1
Action Minutes
May 15, 2018
 2.  CDP-111-18; Consideration of a Coastal Development Permit Application for yard
  improvements at the single family residence located at 2100 Rosita Place. Lot 1 & a portion
  of Lot F, Block 2, Tract 10624. This project is exempt from CEQA pursuant to California
  Administrative Code Title 14, Chapter 3, Section 15303.

  Applicant:  Alan McGregor
  16332 Bradbury Lane
  Huntington Beach, CA 92647
  Owner:  Ed & Marcia Dawson

  Action: Commissioner Chang moved and Commissioner Criley seconded to approve the
  application (5-0 in favor) with standard conditions and the following additional condition:
  1) The septic system (pipes, tanks, leachfields, etc.) shall be plotted to ensure proposed
  improvements do not adversely impact the system.

3.  M-1263-18; Consideration of a Miscellaneous Application for non-standard encroachments

  application (5-0 in favor) with standard conditions and the following additional condition:
  1) Minor adjustments to the location of the proposed gate and fence may be allowed to

  Applicant:  Tomaro Architecture
  2617 N. Sepulveda Blvd., #100
  Manhattan Beach, CA 90266
  Owner:  William Peckovich

  Speakers: Allan Rigg, Bill Peckovich, Alex Nikolakopulos, Walter Christmas, Louie
  Tomaro
  Action: Commissioner Criley moved and Commissioner Chang seconded to approve the
  application (4-1 in favor, Lazzaro dissenting) with standard conditions and the following
  additional conditions: 1) The second story ridgeline shall be lowered by 1 ft.; 2) The
  chimney shall be lowered by 1 ft.; and 3) The hedge shall be lowered and maintained to a
  maximum height of 12 ft.

  Chairman Thomas moved to rescind the prior motion and Commissioner Chang seconded
  (5-0 in favor).

  Commissioner Criley made a substitute motion and Commissioner Chang seconded to
  approve the application (5-0 in favor) with standard conditions and the following additional
  conditions: 1) The second story ridgeline shall be lowered by 1 ft.; 2) The chimney shall be
  lowered by 1 ft.; and 3) The hedge shall be lowered and maintained to a maximum height of
  16 ft.

  Janine Nendick, Vi Ballard, Walburga Meschuk, Ruth Harnack, Tina Saxe, Wade Welch
  Continued to the July 19th Planning Commission meeting.

PUBLIC HEARING

8.  Zone Text Amendment to the City’s municipal code amending sections 17.08, 18.04.130
  and 18.08.010 to define Accessory Dwelling Unit and Junior Accessory Dwelling Unit, to
  establish procedures and standards for accessory dwelling units and junior accessory
  dwelling units in the R-1 single family residential and R-M multiple family residential
  zones, and to otherwise conform with state law.

  Speakers: Janine Nendick, Marlene Breene
  Action: Commissioner Chang moved and Chairman Thomas seconded to recommend
  approval to the City Council the proposed ordinance (5-0 in favor) with the following
  additional amendments: 1) Incorporating a provision for lots that are over 15,000 sq. ft. that
  they demonstrate they are able to provide sufficient on-site parking. If they do not provide
  sufficient on-site parking and the property is located on a street that is of a width that would
  allow restricted parking to be on one side of the street, the the property is not eligible to be
  approved administratively and shall be deferred to the Planning Commission; and 2) The
  word “significant” shall be added to the required findings in Section 5(B)(5)(5) and Section
  5(C)(4)(5).

Planning Commission  4

May 15, 2018
